newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Monetary Authority considers joining IMF fund.
newsitem.headline: HK's Monetary Authority considers joining IMF fund.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) was considering joining the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) planned new emergency fund next year, the authority's chief executive said on Wednesday.
"The HKMA is considering whether to participate in this new arrangement," said Joseph Yam, chief executive of the HKMA. "Our total contribution would not be more than US$500 million."
Membership in the IMF's New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB) would be one of the major tasks of the authority in 1997, the head of Hong Kong's defacto central bank told a news conference.
The new IMF agreement must still be approved by individual countries, including Hong Kong, and by the executive board of the IMF, which is to meet next in January 1997, Yam added.

At the IMF/World Bank meeting that closed in October, the Group of 10 industrialised countries reached a basic agreement with rapidly developing countries on a plan to double the IMF's emergency resources.
The plan is aimed at boosting the money the IMF can draw on in financial emergencies to about US$50 billion through the creation of the NAB.

Australia, Austria, Finland, Malaysia, Norway, Singapore, South Korea, Spain and Thailand had committed themselves to joining the NAB, while Chile and Hong Kong were among those still holding talks about their possible participation.
The 11-nation G10 comprises Belgium, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the United States.
